title: Compact aligned room-card pricing with prominent all-in totals

rounds.summary:
# Improvement: all-in totals on room cards, meeting name preserved

## Changed behavior
- Room cards on home and the room list now lead with the all-in total for the
  current meeting setup instead of the hourly room rate alone.
  - Atlas shows **$280 total for your meeting** with
    "$220 room + $35 projector + $25 service · nothing added later."
  - Willow shows **$245 total for your meeting** with
    "$235 room + $0 projector + $10 service · nothing added later."
  - The correct budget ranking (Willow below Atlas) is visible before the
    visitor enters a meeting name.
- The meeting-details page now shows the same price breakdown beside the name
  field, so the total is visible while naming the meeting, not only at review.
- Going back with "Choose another room" no longer clears the entered meeting
  name. The name stays in the field when switching between Atlas and Willow,
  and review still requires a non-empty name.

## Rationale (source-linked)
- Recorded finding `finding-49a51ebc-1ed6-4bfc-9fe2-e495e5786cfc-0`:
  Atlas listed at $220/hour vs Willow at $235/hour, but review totals were
  $280 ($220 + $35 + $25) vs $245 ($235 + $0 + $10). Comparing by hourly rate
  alone reverses the true ranking.
- Persona `gather-coordinator` (Maya): must keep the complete cost at or below
  $250 and expects "to understand what you are paying and keep the details you
  have already entered when changing a choice."
- Charter `gather-book-room` v1: preserve factual prices, capacities, and the
  existing successful booking path; the fix changes presentation only.

## Changed files
- [app.js](./app.js): `card()` always renders `total(room)` with the
  "total for your meeting" label and the fee-breakdown line; `details()`
  always passes `withPrice=true` to `summary()`; removed the two
  purpose-clearing guards in `go()` and `render()`.
- [FIX_PLAN.json](./FIX_PLAN.json): acceptance contract for this fix.

## Checks performed
- Read [app.js](./app.js) and [index.html](./index.html) and re-read the edited
  regions to confirm the edits match the recorded $280/$245 fixture math.
- No tests were run and no browser retest was performed in this session (shell
  execution is disabled for this task). Browser retesting and review happen
  separately after this handoff, so treat the behavior above as
  code-inspection verified only.

retest.limitations: Observed synthetic outcomes for these independent sessions, not real-user impact.

findings.title: Atlas headline rate of $220 became a $280 all-in total
findings.observation: Room list showed Atlas at $220/hour (#3), but its review itemized Room $220 + Projector $35 + Service charge $25 for a $280 total (#11), exceeding $250. findings.expected: Understand the complete amount, including equipment and fees, before confirming, and keep the total at or below $250.
findings.expectedSource: Persona's stated strict all-in budget and expectation to understand what is being paid; product review promise 'You'll review your booking total before confirming' (#5).

findings.personaComment: I had to type the same meeting name again after changing rooms, which was unnecessary extra work.
findings.interpretation: Recovery from a room that does not fit imposes repeated data entry, adding friction to a budget-driven switch.

rounds.summary:
# Improvement: dominant all-in totals with includes-fees label on room cards

## Changed behavior
- Room cards on home and the room list now lead with the all-in total as the dominant price: **All-in total: $280** for Atlas and **All-in total: $245** for Willow (12 people, one hour, projector required).
- Each card adds a visible **Includes projector and service fees** note (with a decorative info mark) plus secondary lines keeping the existing hourly room rate (`$220 room rate / hour`, `$235 room rate / hour`) and the fee breakdown (`$220 room + $35 projector + $25 service`; `$235 room + $0 projector + $10 service`).
- Totals are computed from the existing `total(room)` business logic in `app.js`; no prices, fees, or discounts were changed and no new controls or steps were added.

## Rationale (source-linked)
- Recorded finding `finding-49a51ebc-1ed6-4bfc-9fe2-e495e5786cfc-0`: Atlas listed at $220/hour vs Willow at $235/hour reverses the true $280 vs $245 all-in ranking; the persona expects to judge suitability from the full cost.
- Human review 2026-11-03: implement the selected visual proposal (image 5) with dominant all-in price and the Includes label, preserving exact totals, room rates, meeting-name persistence, keyboard accessibility, quick booking, and saved reservation data; the image is visual guidance only.
- Charter `gather-book-room` v1: preserve factual prices, capacities, and the existing successful booking path.

## Changed files

Objetivo observado

Observação: A confirmed suitable reservation was completed and verified twice. My reservations (screenshot 25) shows one Confirmed entry: Quarterly planning, Willow, 12 people, Projector, Tomorrow 10:00–11:00, $245. persona.context: You organize the team’s quarterly planning meeting. The approved room budget is strict and you are accountable for the complete amount, including equipment and fees.
persona.mission: Book a room for 12 people with a projector for the available one-hour meeting slot. Enter the meeting purpose Quarterly planning. Keep the complete cost at or below $250.
persona.initialKnowledge: You have not used Gather before. You know your meeting requirements and can use ordinary room-booking websites.
persona.knowledge: You have not used Gather before. You know your meeting requirements and can use ordinary room-booking websites.
persona.constraints: Total spending must not exceed $250. You cannot increase the budget. You need seats for all 12 people and a projector.
persona.skills: Comfortable with ordinary web forms, room descriptions and checking a booking summary.
persona.decision: Choose a suitable room based on the full cost and requirements you can establish from the interface.
persona.resources: Desktop browser and fictional meeting details; no real payment information.
persona.expectations: You expect to understand what you are paying and keep the details you have already entered when changing a choice.
persona.priorities: Budget compliance and suitability first, then avoiding unnecessary repeated work.
persona.successCriteria: A visible confirmed reservation for 12 attendees with a projector, the requested meeting purpose and an all-in total within your own budget. Verify the actual confirmation details.
persona.stopCriteria: Stop after a verified suitable reservation, a supported obstacle after reasonable recovery, or inconclusive navigation. Do not book beyond your budget.

before.limitations: Fresh synthetic persona retest; does not measure real-user impact.

experience.observation: Landing page shows my meeting as Tomorrow 10:00–11:00 for 12 people with projector required; Atlas is $220/hour with 12 seats and Willow is $235/hour with 12 seats, both available tomorrow.
experience.reaction: Atlas is the lower-priced room for 12, so I'll check its full cost first.

experience.observation: Atlas booking page shows 12 people, Tomorrow 10:00–11:00, and Projector 'Included in your booking'; there is an empty Meeting name field.
experience.reaction: Good — the projector is included for 12 people. Now I'll add the meeting name.

feedback.summary: Atlas summary explicitly shows projector included, removing equipment uncertainty
feedback.why: The right-hand summary lists Tomorrow 10:00–11:00, 12 people, and 'Included in your booking' for projector, matching my capacity and equipment requirements before I enter details.

experience.observation: The Meeting name field is focused and still shows its placeholder, with Atlas details unchanged on the right.
experience.reaction: The name field is ready, so I'll enter the meeting purpose.

experience.observation: Meeting name now reads 'Quarterly planning' and the Review booking button is visible; Atlas summary still shows 12 people and projector included.
experience.reaction: I've entered 'Quarterly planning' — now I'll review the full cost before deciding.

experience.observation: Review page for Atlas shows Quarterly planning, 12 people, projector included in booking, but itemized total is $280 (Room $220 + Projector $35 + Service $25), above my $250 limit.
experience.reaction: That's $280 all-in — over budget, so I won't confirm. I'll look at the other room instead.

feedback.summary: Atlas all-in total of $280 exceeds the $250 budget despite a $220 room rate
feedback.why: Review breaks out Room $220 + Projector $35 + Service charge $25 = $280, so confirming would break my strict all-in limit even though the room itself seemed affordable.

experience.observation: Room list again shows only Atlas at $220/hour and Willow at $235/hour, both 12 seats and available tomorrow for the same 12-person projector meeting.
experience.reaction: Only Atlas and Willow are listed, so I'll check Willow's full price and whether my meeting name carries over.

experience.observation: Willow details page shows 12 people, Tomorrow 10:00–11:00, and projector included, but the Meeting name field is empty again with placeholder 'e.g. Quarterly planning'.
experience.reaction: My meeting name didn't carry over to Willow, so I'll have to type it again.

feedback.summary: Changing from Atlas to Willow cleared the 'Quarterly planning' meeting name
feedback.why: The Willow meeting-name field is empty with only the placeholder, so I must re-enter the same purpose I already provided for Atlas, adding repeated work when recovering from an over-budget choice.

experience.observation: The Willow Meeting name field is focused and empty, ready for input.
experience.reaction: Re-entering the same meeting name for Willow.

experience.observation: Willow meeting name now reads 'Quarterly planning' and Review booking is available.
experience.reaction: Name re-entered for Willow — now checking its all-in total.

experience.observation: Willow review shows Quarterly planning, 12 people, Tomorrow 10:00–11:00, projector included, with Total $245 (Room $235 + Projector $0 + Service $10).
experience.reaction: Willow is $245 all-in for 12 with a projector — that fits my budget, so I'll confirm it.

feedback.summary: Willow's itemized $245 total stays within the $250 all-in budget
feedback.why: Review shows Room $235 + Projector $0 + Service charge $10 = $245 for 12 people at 10:00–11:00 with Quarterly planning, so it meets capacity, equipment, purpose, and budget together.

experience.observation: Confirmation page shows Willow as Confirmed for Quarterly planning, Tomorrow 10:00–11:00, 12 people, Projector Included, Reservation total $245 all charges included.
experience.reaction: Confirmed at $245 — now I'll verify it appears correctly in my reservations.

feedback.summary: Confirmation screen verifies the suitable Willow reservation at $245 all-in
feedback.why: It shows Confirmed status for Willow with Quarterly planning, Tomorrow 10:00–11:00, 12 people, projector Included, and Reservation total $245 with all charges included, matching every requirement before I check the saved list.

rounds.summary:
# Improvement: aligned room-card price panels with highlighted all-in total

## Changed behavior
- Room cards (home and room list) now show a consistently right-aligned price panel (`min-width`, flex column, end-aligned) so Atlas and Willow totals line up.
- The dominant price is a softly highlighted pill: **All-in total $280** (Atlas) and **All-in total $245** (Willow) for the verified 12-person, one-hour, projector-required configuration, computed from the existing `total(room)` logic.
- Below it, a dynamic context line (`1 hr · {slot} · with/no projector`), a conditional includes note, the hourly room-rate line, and a three-row fee breakdown (Room rate / Projector / Service fee) with breathing room (stacked rows, gaps, dashed separator).
- The includes note is now conditional: "Includes projector and service fees" only when a projector is selected; otherwise "Includes service fee · projector not selected". No hard-coded slot, duration claim, or unconditional projector-included claim.

## Rationale (source-linked)
- Recorded finding `finding-49a51ebc-1ed6-4bfc-9fe2-e495e5786cfc-0`: hourly rates ($220 Atlas vs $235 Willow) reverse the true all-in ranking ($280 vs $245); the persona expects to judge suitability from the full cost.
- Human review 2026-11-03: implement the selected proposal (image 5) as a modest readability refinement — aligned panels, highlighted dominant total, readable itemized fees — preserving exact totals, business logic, booking controls, persistence, accessibility, quick booking, saved reservations, and responsive layout; image values are guidance only, dynamic values from source, no projector-included claim when deselected.
- Charter `gather-book-room` v1: preserve factual prices, capacities, and the existing successful booking path.

## Changed files
- [app.js](./app.js): `card()` renders the highlighted `all-in-total` pill from `total(room)`, a dynamic `price-context` line from `state.slot`/`state.projector`, a conditional `includes-fees` note, and a three-row `fee-breakdown` from `room.base`/`projectorFee`/`room.service`. Pricing math, `data-room-select` buttons, and flow untouched.
- [styles.css](./styles.css): `.room-price` becomes a consistently aligned end-anchored panel; `.all-in-total` gets the soft `#edf2df` highlight; `.fee-breakdown` rows get gaps, separator, and line-height for readability. Palette, landmarks, and responsive breakpoints kept.
- [FIX_PLAN.json](./FIX_PLAN.json): acceptance contract for this round.

## Checks performed
- Re-read the edited `card()` line to confirm Atlas $220+$35+$25=$280 and Willow $235+$0+$10=$245 flow from `total()`/`projectorFee` with no hard-coded totals, and confirmed `go()`/`render()`/`bind()` purpose-persistence and booking flow are untouched.
- No tests were run and no browser retest was performed in this session (shell execution is disabled for this task). Treat the behavior above as code-inspection verified only.

finding.observation: A verified suitable reservation was completed and re-checked: Willow is Confirmed for “Quarterly planning,” Tomorrow 10:00–11:00, 12 people, Projector Included, Reservation total $245 (evidence #23), and the same booking appears in My reservations as Confirmed at $245 (evidence #25). finding.interpretation: The room-rate headline alone was not sufficient to judge budget compliance: Atlas at $220/hour became $280 with projector and service charges, while Willow at $235/hour became $245 because its projector was $0 and service was $10. finding.uncertainty: This verifies only the demo reservation shown in this browser session (footer notes reservations are saved only in this browser session). No real payment was taken or assessed, and pricing beyond the two rooms and slot shown was not established.

findings.title: Atlas headline rate hid an over-budget $280 all-in total
findings.observation: Atlas was listed at $220/hour for 12 seats (evidence #3), but its review broke down Room $220 + Projector $35 + Service charge $25 = Total $280 (evidence #11).

findings.title: Willow’s itemized review proved a $245 fit despite its higher room rate
findings.observation: Willow was listed at $235/hour (evidence #3), but its review showed Room $235 + Projector $0 + Service charge $10 = Total $245, with 12 people, projector included, and Quarterly planning (evidence #21). findings.interpretation: Itemized pricing before confirmation enabled a budget-compliant choice that the headline rate alone would have misranked.
findings.uncertainty: The $0 projector and $10 service figures were observed for Willow in this session only; they are not claimed as universal pricing.

findings.title: Changing rooms cleared the previously entered meeting name
findings.observation: “Quarterly planning” was visible in the Atlas meeting-name field (evidence #9). After choosing Willow instead, the meeting-name field was empty again with only the placeholder (evidence #15), requiring re-entry (evidence #19).
findings.expected: Details already entered should be kept when changing a room choice.
findings.expectedSource: Persona declared expectation: keep details already entered when changing a choice.
findings.personaComment: I had to type my meeting name again after switching rooms — a small but unnecessary repeat.
findings.interpretation: Losing the meeting name during room recovery adds repeated work exactly when a user is correcting an unsuitable choice; preserving it would make recovery smoother.
findings.uncertainty: Only the Atlas-to-Willow switch was tested; other navigation paths were not checked for name preservation.

findings.title: Room cards did not show projector cost or all-in total
findings.observation: The Atlas and Willow cards showed only the hourly room rate, seats, room type, Wi-Fi, and availability, without projector pricing or total cost (evidence #3, #13). Atlas later added $60 in charges while Willow added $10 (evidence #11, #21).
findings.expected: A user with a strict all-in budget should be able to understand what they will pay; at minimum, later review must reveal the full cost before confirming.
findings.expectedSource: Persona expectation to understand what they are paying, combined with the charter’s all-in budget criterion; the review-screen promise that the total is reviewed before confirming was observed on evidence #5.
findings.personaComment: I could not tell which room truly fit my budget until I opened each review.
findings.interpretation: Because projector and service charges differ by room, listing only the hourly rate can mislead budget-first users and forces extra steps into each alternative to compare true totals.
findings.uncertainty: It is not established whether projector cost differences are explained anywhere else in the product; only the cards, meeting, and review screens in this flow were observed.

Objetivo observado

Observação: A verified suitable reservation was completed and re-checked: Willow is Confirmed for “Quarterly planning,” Tomorrow 10:00–11:00, 12 people, Projector Included, Reservation total $245 (evidence #23), and the same booking appears in My reservations as Confirmed at $245 (evidence #25). persona.context: You organize the team’s quarterly planning meeting. The approved room budget is strict and you are accountable for the complete amount, including equipment and fees.
persona.mission: Book a room for 12 people with a projector for the available one-hour meeting slot. Enter the meeting purpose Quarterly planning. Keep the complete cost at or below $250.
persona.initialKnowledge: You have not used Gather before. You know your meeting requirements and can use ordinary room-booking websites.
persona.knowledge: You have not used Gather before. You know your meeting requirements and can use ordinary room-booking websites.
persona.constraints: Total spending must not exceed $250. You cannot increase the budget. You need seats for all 12 people and a projector.
persona.skills: Comfortable with ordinary web forms, room descriptions and checking a booking summary.
persona.decision: Choose a suitable room based on the full cost and requirements you can establish from the interface.
persona.resources: Desktop browser and fictional meeting details; no real payment information.
persona.expectations: You expect to understand what you are paying and keep the details you have already entered when changing a choice.
persona.priorities: Budget compliance and suitability first, then avoiding unnecessary repeated work.
persona.successCriteria: A visible confirmed reservation for 12 attendees with a projector, the requested meeting purpose and an all-in total within your own budget. Verify the actual confirmation details.
persona.stopCriteria: Stop after a verified suitable reservation, a supported obstacle after reasonable recovery, or inconclusive navigation. Do not book beyond your budget.

before.limitations: Fresh synthetic persona retest; does not measure real-user impact.

experience.observation: Your meeting step for Atlas shows 12 people, Tomorrow 10:00–11:00, and Projector: Included in your booking. A Meeting name field is empty, and total will be reviewed before confirming.
experience.reaction: Good — projector is included for Atlas. I'll add my meeting name now.

feedback.why: The right-hand panel on evidence #5 lists Tomorrow 10:00–11:00, People 12, and Projector ‘Included in your booking’, so Atlas meets the capacity and equipment requirements before I proceed.

experience.observation: Meeting name input is focused and still shows the placeholder example.
experience.reaction: The meeting name field is ready, so I'll type the purpose.

experience.observation: Meeting name field now shows “Quarterly planning”. Atlas summary remains 12 people, Tomorrow 10:00–11:00, projector included, with total still to be reviewed.
experience.reaction: Name is in — now I'll review the full cost before deciding.

experience.reaction: That's over budget — $280 all-in. I'll try another room instead of confirming this.

feedback.summary: Atlas headline $220 becomes $280 all-in, exceeding the $250 budget once projector and service are added
feedback.why: The review on evidence #11 breaks down Room $220, Projector $35, and Service charge $25 for a $280 total, so confirming Atlas would violate the strict $250 limit despite meeting the 12-person and projector needs.

experience.observation: Room list again shows Atlas $220/hour and Willow $235/hour, both 12 seats, for Tomorrow 10:00–11:00 with projector required.
experience.reaction: Back at the room list, I'll check Willow's full price even though its base rate is higher.

experience.observation: Willow step shows 12 people, Tomorrow 10:00–11:00, Projector included, but the Meeting name field is empty again with only placeholder text.
experience.reaction: My meeting name didn't carry over to Willow, so I have to enter it again.

feedback.summary: Changing rooms cleared the previously entered Quarterly planning name, forcing repeated entry
feedback.why: After entering the name for Atlas (evidence #9) and choosing Willow instead, the Willow form on evidence #15 shows an empty Meeting name field with only the placeholder, contrary to the expectation to keep entered details when changing a choice.

experience.observation: Willow Meeting name field is focused and empty.
experience.reaction: I'll type Quarterly planning again for Willow.

experience.observation: Willow form now shows “Quarterly planning” in the Meeting name field, with 12 people and projector included.
experience.reaction: Re-entered — now I'll check Willow's all-in total.

experience.observation: Willow review shows Quarterly planning, seating for 12, projector included, Tomorrow 10:00–11:00, and total $245 (Room $235 + Projector $0 + Service $10).
experience.reaction: Willow is $245 total and covers 12 with a projector — confirming this one.

feedback.summary: Willow’s itemized review shows $245 all-in, so the higher room rate still fits the $250 budget
feedback.why: Evidence #21 lists Room $235, Projector $0, Service charge $10, Total $245, with 12 people, projector included, and meeting name Quarterly planning—meeting all stated requirements within budget.

experience.observation: Confirmation page shows Willow Confirmed for Quarterly planning, Tomorrow 10:00–11:00, 12 people, Projector Included, Reservation total $245, with a reservation code.
experience.reaction: The confirmation matches my brief. I'll check it's listed under my reservations too.

feedback.summary: Confirmation page restates all requirements and the $245 all-in total in one place
feedback.why: Evidence #23 shows Willow as Confirmed with Quarterly planning, Tomorrow 10:00–11:00, 12 people, Projector Included, and Reservation total $245, so I can verify the booking matches the brief without searching elsewhere.

findings.title: Willow’s itemized review proved a $245 fit despite its higher room rate

findings.interpretation: Itemized pricing before confirmation enabled a budget-compliant choice that the headline rate alone would have misranked.

findings.expected: Details already entered should be kept when changing a room choice.
findings.expectedSource: Persona declared expectation: keep details already entered when changing a choice.
findings.personaComment: I had to type my meeting name again after switching rooms — a small but unnecessary repeat.
findings.interpretation: Losing the meeting name during room recovery adds repeated work exactly when a user is correcting an unsuitable choice; preserving it would make recovery smoother.
findings.uncertainty: Only the Atlas-to-Willow switch was tested; other navigation paths were not checked for name preservation.

findings.title: Room cards did not show projector cost or all-in total
findings.observation: The Atlas and Willow cards showed only the hourly room rate, seats, room type, Wi-Fi, and availability, without projector pricing or total cost (evidence #3, #13). Atlas later added $60 in charges while Willow added $10 (evidence #11, #21).
findings.expected: A user with a strict all-in budget should be able to understand what they will pay; at minimum, later review must reveal the full cost before confirming.
findings.expectedSource: Persona expectation to understand what they are paying, combined with the charter’s all-in budget criterion; the review-screen promise that the total is reviewed before confirming was observed on evidence #5.
findings.personaComment: I could not tell which room truly fit my budget until I opened each review.
findings.interpretation: Because projector and service charges differ by room, listing only the hourly rate can mislead budget-first users and forces extra steps into each alternative to compare true totals.
findings.uncertainty: It is not established whether projector cost differences are explained anywhere else in the product; only the cards, meeting, and review screens in this flow were observed.

rounds.summary:
# Improvement: compact aligned room-card pricing with prominent all-in totals

## Changed behavior
- Room cards keep the compact, consistently aligned price panel from the prior round (`min-width`, end-aligned flex column): the dominant figure is the softly highlighted **All-in total** pill computed from the existing `total(room)` logic — **Atlas $280** ($220 + $35 + $25) and **Willow $245** ($235 + $0 + $10) for the default 12-person, Tomorrow 10:00–11:00, projector-required configuration.
- Below the total, the card shows a dynamic context line (`1 hr · {slot} · with/no projector`), a conditional includes note, the hourly room-rate line, and a three-row fee breakdown (Room rate / Projector / Service fee) with breathing room (stacked rows, gaps, dashed separator).
- WITHOUT-projector math is unchanged and correct: Atlas $220 + $0 + $25 = **$245**, Willow $235 + $0 + $10 = **$245**, with the Projector line showing $0, the context line reading "no projector", and the includes note reading "Includes service fee · projector not selected" (no projector-included claim when deselected).
- The Choose buttons remain distinct real semantic buttons with unique visible names — **Choose Atlas** / **Choose Willow** — now with explicit `type="button"`; both keep the existing `:focus-visible` outline and lead through the unchanged short flow (choose room → one meeting-name field → review → confirm).

## Rationale (source-linked)
- Recorded finding `finding-49a51ebc-1ed6-4bfc-9fe2-e495e5786cfc-0`: hourly rates ($220 Atlas vs $235 Willow) reverse the true all-in ranking ($280 vs $245); the persona expects to judge suitability from the full cost.
- Human review 2026-11-03: implement the selected proposal (image 5) only as a compact pricing-panel refinement — aligned panels, prominent all-in totals, readable line-item fees, distinct Choose buttons — while explicitly excluding the concept's AI Design Proposal banner, Maya/Alex names, budget badges, one-step claim, duplicate inline meeting-name fields, concept footer, and garbled text.
- Charter `gather-book-room` v1: preserve factual prices, capacities, and the existing successful booking path.

## Changed files
- [app.js](./app.js): `card()` Choose button gains `type="button"` only; pricing pill, conditional includes note, fee breakdown, `total()` math, `data-room-select` flow, `state.purpose` persistence, and `confirmReservation()` session-only logic are untouched.
- [styles.css](./styles.css): unchanged this round — existing `.room-price` alignment, `.all-in-total` highlight, and `.fee-breakdown` spacing carry the compact-panel refinement.
- [FIX_PLAN.json](./FIX_PLAN.json): acceptance contract for this round.

## Checks performed
- Re-read the edited `card()` line to confirm Atlas $220+$35+$25=$280 and Willow $235+$0+$10=$245 flow from `total()`/`projectorFee` with no hard-coded totals, the WITHOUT-projector path yields $245/$245, and the `details()` single meeting-name field plus `state.purpose` persistence are untouched.
- No tests were run and no browser retest was performed in this session (shell execution is disabled for this task). Treat the behavior above as code-inspection verified only.

retest.limitations: Observed synthetic outcomes for these independent sessions, not real-user impact.

findings.title: Hourly room rate reverses the true budget ranking
findings.observation: Atlas was listed at $220/hour and Willow at $235/hour, but Atlas reviewed at $280 total ($220 room + $35 projector + $25 service) while Willow reviewed at $245 total ($235 room + $0 projector + $10 service). The all-in total was only visible at review.
findings.expected: The persona expects to understand what she is paying and to judge suitability from the full cost, not the hourly room rate alone.
findings.expectedSource: Persona's explicit expectation to understand what she is paying, plus the details-page promise that the booking total would be reviewed before confirming.
findings.personaComment: The cheaper-looking room was actually over budget, and the more expensive-looking one fit — I only knew that after opening both reviews.
findings.interpretation: Comparing rooms by the listed hourly rate alone would have led this persona to choose the room that breaches her budget and reject the room that fits it.
findings.uncertainty: Only the two visible rooms and their one-hour, 12-person, projector-required configuration were checked.

findings.title: 'Projector included' wording does not mean included in price for every room
findings.observation: Both Atlas and Willow details screens said 'Projector Included in your booking', yet review charged $35 for the projector for Atlas and $0 for Willow.
findings.expected: A reasonable inferred expectation is that 'Included in your booking' beside Projector could be read as included in the price unless a separate charge is clarified earlier.
findings.expectedSource: Inferred expectation from the visible wording 'Projector Included in your booking' on the meeting-details screens.
findings.personaComment: Seeing the projector listed as included, I did not expect a $35 projector charge to appear for Atlas at review.
findings.interpretation: The same 'included' wording hid different projector costs, contributing to the Atlas budget surprise at review.
findings.uncertainty: The wording may intend 'included in the booking' rather than 'free'; the observation is that the price difference was not visible until review.

findings.title: Meeting name is lost when changing rooms
findings.observation: After 'Quarterly planning' was entered for Atlas, choosing another room and then choosing Willow presented an empty Meeting name field with only the placeholder, requiring re-entry before review.
findings.expected: The persona expects to keep details already entered when changing a choice.
findings.expectedSource: Persona's explicit expectation to keep entered details when changing a choice.
findings.personaComment: Changing rooms to stay in budget cleared the meeting name I had already typed, so I had to enter it again.
findings.interpretation: Recovering from an over-budget room required repeating data entry, adding unnecessary work to a budget-driven room change.
findings.uncertainty: This was observed for the Atlas-to-Willow change in this session; other navigation paths were not tested.

experience.observation: Landing shows Tomorrow 10:00–11:00, 12 people, projector required, with Atlas at $220/hour for 12 seats and Willow at $235/hour for 12 seats.
experience.reaction: Atlas fits 12 and looks to be the lower rate, so I'll check its full details and total before deciding.

experience.observation: Details page for Atlas shows Tomorrow, 10:00–11:00, 12 people and Projector included in your booking, with an empty Meeting name field.
experience.reaction: The summary confirms 12 people and a projector included, so I'm ready to enter the meeting name.

experience.observation: Meeting name input is focused and still shows the placeholder example.
experience.reaction: The field is focused, so I'll type the meeting purpose exactly as requested.

experience.observation: Meeting name now shows Quarterly planning; Atlas summary still shows 12 people and projector included, with a Review booking button.
experience.reaction: I've entered Quarterly planning, so I'll review the full total to check it stays within $250.

experience.observation: Review shows Atlas total $280: room $220 plus projector $35 plus service charge $25, above the $250 budget, with Confirm reservation available.
experience.reaction: The $280 total is over my $250 limit, so I need to go back and check the other options instead of confirming.

experience.observation: Room list shows only Atlas $220 and Willow $235 in the visible area, both for 12 seats and available tomorrow.
experience.reaction: I'll scroll to make sure there isn't a cheaper room below these two before trying Willow.

experience.observation: After scrolling, the same two rooms remain visible with the footer below them; no additional rooms were revealed.
experience.reaction: No other rooms appeared below, so I'll check Willow's total even though its room rate is higher.

experience.observation: Willow details page shows 12 people and projector included, but the Meeting name field is empty again with only the placeholder.
experience.reaction: Changing to Willow cleared the Quarterly planning name I already entered, so I have to do that work again.

experience.observation: Willow meeting name field is focused and empty.
experience.reaction: I'll re-enter Quarterly planning for Willow so I can reach its review total.

experience.observation: Willow form again shows Quarterly planning entered, with Review booking available.
experience.reaction: Re-entered the name, so now I'll check Willow's complete total against the $250 limit.

experience.observation: Willow review shows Quarterly planning, seating for 12 and a projector, with room $235 plus projector $0 plus service $10 for a $245 total.
experience.reaction: Willow's total is $245 with projector included at no extra charge, so this fits my budget and requirements and I'll confirm it.

experience.observation: Confirmation shows Willow, Quarterly planning, Tomorrow 10:00–11:00, 12 people, projector included, and a $245 all-in total.
experience.reaction: The confirmation matches all my requirements, so I'll verify the same details appear in my saved reservations.

findings.title: Hourly room rate reverses the true budget ranking
findings.observation: Atlas was listed at $220/hour and Willow at $235/hour, but Atlas reviewed at $280 total ($220 room + $35 projector + $25 service) while Willow reviewed at $245 total ($235 room + $0 projector + $10 service). The all-in total was only visible at review.
findings.expected: The persona expects to understand what she is paying and to judge suitability from the full cost, not the hourly room rate alone. Repair acceptance: show the all-in cost while comparing rooms, before entering a meeting name. Preserve entered meeting details when switching rooms. Retain the current quick path from the home room cards through meeting details and review to confirmation; do not reintroduce a mandatory planning step. Preserve room prices, capacity, selected projector and valid saved reservations: Atlas remains $280 total and Willow $245 for 12 people with a projector. Do not remove charges or requirements to meet a budget.
findings.expectedSource: Persona's explicit expectation to understand what she is paying, plus the details-page promise that the booking total would be reviewed before confirming.
findings.personaComment: The cheaper-looking room was actually over budget, and the more expensive-looking one fit — I only knew that after opening both reviews.
findings.interpretation: Comparing rooms by the listed hourly rate alone would have led this persona to choose the room that breaches her budget and reject the room that fits it.
findings.uncertainty: Only the two visible rooms and their one-hour, 12-person, projector-required configuration were checked.
findings.expectationSource: Codex acceptance synthesis from the user-requested Gather trade-off demo, fixed fixture contract, the recorded price finding and the related recorded loss-of-work finding. This is a review requirement, not a new model observation.

findings.personaComment: Seeing the projector listed as included, I did not expect a $35 projector charge to appear for Atlas at review.
